# CMS-DACO: Dynamic ACO for Crowd Evacuation under Spreading Fire (IEEE paper companion)

**PDF:** [`docs/IEEE_Paper.pdf`](IEEE_Paper.pdf) — 5 pages, compiled from `IEEE_Paper.tex` (IEEEtran).
**Full reproducibility:** raw per-seed results, merged summaries, statistics and figure sources live in `cms/experiments/results/` and are generated by the scripts below.

## What this paper is
An *empirical* study of evacuation routing policies on a grid world with a spreading fire/smoke field:

- **Policies compared:** Random walk · BFS-distance greedy · Hazard-aware A\* (per-tick replanning) · Standard ACO · Full CMS-DACO (BFS-seeded pheromone + annealed ants + dual speed/safety channels + predictive congestion + stagnation escape).
- **Conditions:** open grid (15², 30 agents, 8% walls) and hard grid (15% walls, one burning blocked exit, East wind 0.5), tick budget 40.
- **Statistics:** N=30 seeds per cell, 95% CIs, Welch t-tests, Cohen's d.

## Headline measured findings (N=30)
| Policy | Open completion | Hard completion |
|---|---|---|
| Random | 0.130 ± 0.022 | 0.074 ± 0.013 |
| Distance (BFS) | 0.989 ± 0.007 | 0.949 ± 0.022 |
| Hazard-aware A* | **0.998 ± 0.003** | **0.991 ± 0.009** |
| Standard ACO | 0.979 ± 0.016 | 0.939 ± 0.033 |
| Full CMS-DACO | 0.974 ± 0.014 | 0.930 ± 0.033 |

1. Any directed policy beats random by an enormous margin (Cohen's d ≥ 17, p < 10⁻³⁰).
2. Per-tick hazard-aware A* significantly beats Full CMS-DACO in **both** regimes (open: p=0.0036, d=0.81; hard: p=0.0011, d=0.92) at identical information access — cached stigmergy adds detour cost without completion benefit when agents fully observe the map.
3. Component ablations move completion ≤ 1.2 pts (all p ≥ 0.34); sweeps over α, β, ρ, T are flat within CIs → results are not knife-edge tuned.
4. Robustness: graceful degradation with wall density (0.99 → 0.71 at 25% walls); crowd size, wind and grid growth leave completion ~0.96–0.98.

## Reproduce everything
```powershell
cd cms/experiments
python run_baselines.py --mode full_cms_daco --seed-start 1 --seed-end 30   # each policy/chunk
python run_hard_conditions.py --mode full_cms_daco --seed-start 1 --seed-end 30
python run_ablation.py --variant full --seed-start 1 --seed-end 30
python run_sensitivity.py --param ALPHA --value 1.35 --seed-start 1 --seed-end 30
python run_robustness.py --sweep walls --value 0.15 --seed-start 1 --seed-end 30
python run_baselines.py --merge ; python run_ablation.py --merge          # etc.
python compute_stats.py      # Welch t / Cohen's d -> stats_summary.json
python make_figures.py       # -> docs/figures/*.pdf
```

## Scope statement
The fire/smoke layer is a computationally efficient cellular model for stress generation at interactive rates; it is **not** validated against FDS/CFAST and no fire-engineering survival claims are made. Routing-policy conclusions apply to grid worlds with full agent observability; partial-observability / communication-limited regimes are the intended extension target of the released testbed.
